findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by(...) can return nil for a logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL without having a TopicUser row for that topic, for example by visiting /t/.../unsubscribe directly for a topic they never interacted with. The next line calls tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError and a 500. Use TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by, TopicUser.change, or handle nil explicitly.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link interpolation now requires unsubscribe_url from every caller
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation now contains %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder interpolates it whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Only send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other MessageBuilder call with add_unsubscribe_link: true and no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the text or HTML body, breaking those emails. Either provide a default value in MessageBuilder or update all callers.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed via GET without CSRF protection
findings.body: The new route maps GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe to a controller action that mutates TopicUser.notification_level based only on the current session. Because there is no CSRF token or per-message secret, any website visited by a logged-in user can embed an image or request to that URL and silently change their notification level for a topic.

findings.title: No assertion for the new topic unsubscribe URL or controller behavior
findings.body: The spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the MessageBuilder input but still only asserts the existing user_preferences_url appears in the body. It does not check that the topic-specific unsubscribe URL appears in the text or HTML, and there are no specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe or Topic#unsubscribe_url, leaving the new behavior effectively untested.
